name: open-design-agent-kit
description: Pro-grade UI design, built into GitHub Copilot Chat: 270+ design skills, 150+ brand design systems, 160+ remixable examples. No desktop app, no daemon, no API keys. Your agent's own model builds decks, landing pages, and prototypes as real files in your repo.

languageModelTools.name: list_open_design_skills
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists available Open Design skills, design templates, and remixable examples — reusable design-task recipes, rendering styles, and (for 'example' entries) actual starting artifacts (e.g. landing page, pitch deck, dashboard) bundled with this extension. Each result's id is namespaced as 'od:<mode>:<name>' (e.g. 'od:deck:guizang-ppt') where mode is one of: prototype, deck, design-system, image, video, template, utility, audio — pass this full id as skillId to prepare_open_design_brief or remix_open_design_example. Note: mode 'design-system' means a skill that helps AUTHOR a design-system deliverable; it is unrelated to designSystemId, which selects from a separate library of ~150 prebuilt brand design systems. Each result's 'source' field is 'skill', 'design-template', 'example', or 'community' (all interchangeable as skillId) — 'community' entries are fetched at runtime from a separate, unreviewed community repo (awesome-open-design) and should be flagged to the user as such if it matters to their request. Some results include an 'examplePrompt' — a curated, ready-to-use brief — which you should prefer verbatim (or lightly adapted) over inventing your own brief when the user's request closely matches one. A result with remixable: true has an actual rendered starting artifact, bundled inside this server and never a file you can find on disk — prefer remix_open_design_example (which copies it into the workspace for you) over prepare_open_design_brief when the user wants to start from or riff on an existing example. Optionally filter by a free-text query matched against name/description/triggers, an exact mode, an exact source, and/or remixableOnly to see only entries with a rendered starting artifact. SURFACES: when the user names a kind of thing to make — a prototype or landing page, mobile app, slides, document, wireframe, animation, résumé, research synthesis, data report, poster or flier, social post, diagram — call this tool with surface set to that surface's id first (call with surface "list" to see the ids) and pick from its entries; if the surface names a prompt, follow that flow. STUBS: an entry with stub: true only advertises an upstream skill and has no instructions here — never pick one; choose a non-stub entry instead. PAGING: with more than 40 matches the result is { total, offset, nextOffset, modes, note, entries }, 100 compact entries (id, name, one-line summary, mode, source) per page; narrow with mode, source, query or surface for the full entries, or pass nextOffset as offset for the next page. If a query returns few or no results, call this tool again with a broader query or no arguments at all to browse the full catalog — do NOT search the filesystem, grep, or read any file (this catalog is not stored anywhere as a single readable file such as a content.json, index, or schema file; it exists only inside this extension's own runtime and is reachable exclusively through this tool).
languageModelTools.userDescription: Browse Open Design's bundled design skills

query.description: Optional free-text filter, matched against skill name, description, and triggers.

remixableOnly.description: Optional: when true, only return entries with remixable: true (an actual rendered starting artifact to remix).

offset.description: Optional: where a paged listing starts. Pass the previous result's nextOffset for the next page.

surface.description: A kind of thing to make — returns that surface's entries in curated order (the recipe first, then its remixable example; never catalog stubs), plus the surface's own prompt and clarifying questions. Pass "list" to get the surfaces themselves (id, label, description, entryCount) and the goals (plain-language aims such as "Promote an event", each with the surfaces it leads to). Ignores the other filters.

goal.description: A goal id from the "list" result (e.g. "promote-event", "get-hired"): returns the surfaces that goal leads to, in order, the first marked default. Use it when the user said what the design is for but not what kind of thing to make.

languageModelTools.name: list_open_design_design_systems
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists available Open Design design systems — brand-inspired visual token sets (palette, typography, spacing, component rules) bundled with this extension, each with a 'category' (e.g. 'E-Commerce & Retail', 'AI & LLM', 'Fintech & Crypto' — call with no arguments to see which categories are present) and an 'active' flag marking the current active design system, if any. Use this to discover which designSystemId to pass to prepare_open_design_brief, or to check what's currently active before asking the user to repeat it. MOBILE: category 'Mobile Apps' holds systems adapted from real iOS apps (ids ending in '-ios', e.g. 'spotify-ios'). For phone screens prefer them, even over a same-brand web system ('spotify'), which stays the one for web pages. Optionally filter by a free-text query matched against name/summary/category, and/or an exact category. If a query returns few or no results, call this tool again with a broader query or no arguments at all to browse the full catalog — do NOT search the filesystem, grep, or read any file (this catalog is not stored anywhere as a single readable file such as a content.json, index, or schema file; it exists only inside this extension's own runtime and is reachable exclusively through this tool).
languageModelTools.userDescription: Browse Open Design's bundled design systems

query.description: Optional free-text filter, matched against design system name, summary, and category.

category.description: Optional exact category filter, e.g. 'E-Commerce & Retail'.

languageModelTools.name: recommend_open_design_design_systems
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Recommends 3 to 5 Open Design design systems for a design, ranked the same way every time, each with a one-line reason and its look (light or dark, accent, display type, corner shape). Use it before prepare_open_design_brief when the user hasn't named a design system or a look, no design system is active, and they want a new design (not an edit, remix or export). Fill the profile from the request, the conversation and the workspace; leave out what you don't know. If the result includes `questions`, ask them once, in one message, and accept "you pick" (then use the first recommendation). Otherwise use the first recommendation, say which one you used and that they can switch (or browse with the 'OpenDesign: Browse Design Systems' command). Does NOT change the active design system: pass the chosen id to prepare_open_design_brief. Product-named looks (Stripe, Linear…) are recommended only when the user names that product, via likeBrands or the brief.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Recommend a design system for what you're making

moods.description: How it should feel, most important first.

theme.description: Light or dark, only if the user said or the context makes it clear.

likeBrands.description: Products or sites the user wants it to feel like, e.g. ['Notion'].

avoid.description: Design system ids or moods to leave out.

brief.description: The request in the user's words.

languageModelTools.name: read_open_design_source
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Converts a workspace document (DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, PDF, Markdown, text or CSV) into Markdown under the output directory's sources/ folder, extracts its embedded images, and returns an outline (headings with line ranges and sizes), never the full text. Read the returned markdownPath yourself, by line range, for the sections you need. Cached by content hash. Use it to look into a source before deciding how to use it; prepare_open_design_brief with `sources` calls it for you. PDFs need `pdftotext` (poppler); without it the result says to read the PDF with your own tools.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read a document (DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, PDF, Markdown) as source material

path.description: Workspace-relative path of the document, e.g. "docs/q3-report.docx" or "CHANGELOG.md".

languageModelTools.name: prepare_open_design_brief
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Composes generation instructions for an Open Design artifact by combining the chosen skill's workflow, an optional design system's visual tokens, universal craft rules, and the user's brief. Returns an 'instructions' string you must follow, plus a 'suggestedEntryPath' for where to author the artifact's entry file in the current workspace. This tool does NOT write any files — after calling it, author the artifact's entry file (and any supporting files) yourself using your normal file-editing tools, following the returned instructions, then call register_open_design_artifact.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Prepare an Open Design generation brief

skillId.description: A skill id from list_open_design_skills, in its full 'od:<mode>:<name>' form.

designSystemId.description: Optional design system id from list_open_design_design_systems. If omitted, falls back to the current active design system (see set_active_design_system). If given explicitly, it also becomes the new active design system for subsequent requests.

brief.description: The user's design brief / request, in their own words.

collectionId.description: Set this (a slug you derive once from the collection name, reused verbatim on every call) when this artifact is one screen of a multi-screen design collection.

collectionName.description: A short display name for the collection, e.g. "Fintech Onboarding Flow". Required together with collectionId.

screenRole.description: Required together with collectionId — this screen's short role label, e.g. "splash", "value-prop", "checkout".

screenTotal.description: Optional: the total number of screens you've planned for this collection, for an accurate "screen N of M" framing.

sources.description: Workspace paths of documents to build the design from (1–10): reports, specs, spreadsheets, existing decks, or repository files such as CHANGELOG.md or docs/adr/*.md. When given, the instructions add the extracted material, a storyline-first workflow (write outline.md, get the user's approval, then build) and accuracy rules.

format.description: Optional canvas format. Adds a Canvas section with the exact size, units, safe area and, for print, bleed and minimum type size, so any skill can produce a post or poster at that size. Screen: x-image (1600×900), ig-square (1080×1080 per card), ig-portrait (1080×1350), story (1080×1920), xhs-card (1080×1440 per card), yt-thumbnail (1280×720), linkedin-image (1200×627), og-image (1200×630), x-header (1500×500), linkedin-banner (1584×396), email-header (600×200, captured at 2×), and display ads banner-mrec (300×250), banner-leaderboard (728×90), banner-skyscraper (160×600), banner-mobile (320×50), and shop images shop-product (2048×2048), shop-banner (1920×800), shop-collection (1920×600). Print (trim sizes, authored in mm with bleed): a4, a3, a2, a1, a0, a5, a6, a7, letter, tabloid, poster-18x24, poster-24x36, postcard-4x6, business-card, business-card-us, and cards with rounded corners trading-card, tarot-card, mini-card. Pass the same id as format to register_open_design_artifact.

fluid.description: With format (or alone): build a fluid design that reflows to any canvas shape, sized in container units with layout rules for wide and tall shapes; the shape is then picked at export (preset/presets) or in the preview, without regenerating. Default: true for print formats, false for screen formats (social recipes need exact pixels). fluid: true without format uses A3 as the default shape. Use it for posters.

answers.description: Optional: the user's answers to the surface's (and the design-system recommender's) questions, by question id, e.g. { "where": "Printed" }. Written into the instructions as decisions to build to.

assumptions.description: Optional: what you decided without asking, up to six short lines, e.g. ["dark theme", "one sign-up button"]. Written into the instructions; list them to the user in one sentence when the design is ready.

languageModelTools.name: prepare_open_design_exploration
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use INSTEAD of prepare_open_design_brief when the user explicitly asks for options, directions, alternatives or several versions of a design. Assigns 2–4 deliberately different directions (visual styles when no design system is active, layout/narrative structures when one is, or labels you pass for a named axis), writes the exploration's plan, and returns sharedInstructions plus one short instructions block, entry path and directionId per direction. Directions are quick sketches; only the one the user picks is built out. Writes no design files: write each direction yourself (follow sharedInstructions + that direction's instructions), register it with explorationId and directionId, then call compare_open_design_exploration. STYLE TILES: with skillId od:design-system:style-tile the directions are compact color + type tiles (default 4, visual axis even with an active design system; axis "custom" with an active system evolves it). Choosing one with next "save-design-system" copies the tile's tokens verbatim.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Plan several different design directions to compare

skillId.description: A skill id from list_open_design_skills, in its full 'od:<mode>:<name>' form.

brief.description: The user's design brief / request, in their own words.

count.description: How many directions: 2–4, default 3; for the style-tile skill 2–6, default 4.

axis.description: What the directions differ in. Omit for the default: 'structure' when a design system is active (brand stays fixed), otherwise 'visual'. 'visual' with an active design system sets that system aside for this exploration. 'custom' needs customDirections.

directionIds.description: Optional: pick specific directions instead of the default order. Visual ids: modern-minimal, human-approachable, tech-utility, editorial-monocle (editorial/publishing briefs), brutalist-experimental (art, agency, manifesto). Structure ids for pages: classic-hero-grid, story-led-scroll, product-ui-first, dense-utility; for decks: problem-solution, narrative-journey, data-led, demo-first.

customDirections.description: For a user-named axis (e.g. "three hero concepts"): 2–4 directions (style tiles: up to 6), each a distinct label and a one-paragraph brief.

designSystemId.description: Optional design system id. If omitted, the active one is used. If given, it also becomes the active one.

languageModelTools.name: compare_open_design_exploration
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Call after registering an exploration's directions. Refreshes and returns the path of its comparison page (compare.html: every direction side by side, opens in any browser from the file system), lists registered and missing directions, and with contactSheet: true renders a PNG of the comparison with the installed browser. If you can view images, check the contact sheet that the directions really differ before showing the user.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Compare an exploration's directions side by side

contactSheet.description: Also render the comparison page to exports/contact-sheet.png. Default false.

languageModelTools.name: choose_open_design_direction
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Call when the user picks a direction from an exploration. Records the choice (marked on the comparison page) and returns instructions for the next step: 'build-out' builds the chosen sketch out at full fidelity, 'merge' does the same while taking named aspects from other directions (needs mergeFrom), and 'save-design-system' turns the direction into a reusable custom design system. Writes no design files.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Take a chosen direction forward

directionId.description: The chosen direction id. It must already be registered.

next.description: What to do with the chosen direction.

notes.description: Optional: the user's own adjustments, in their words.

aspect.description: What to take, e.g. "hero", "colour palette", "pricing table".

mergeFrom.description: Required for 'merge': which aspects to take from which other directions.

languageModelTools.name: register_open_design_artifact
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Call this AFTER you have written an artifact's entry file (and any supporting files) into the workspace with your normal file-editing tools. Validates the artifact and writes its manifest sidecar (<entry>.artifact.json) next to the entry file, so it's recognized as an Open Design artifact. Fails clearly if entryPath does not exist yet — write the file first.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Register a generated file as an Open Design artifact

entryPath.description: Workspace-relative path to the artifact's entry file, e.g. .open-design/coffee-landing/index.html.

title.description: A short human-readable title for the artifact.

supportingFiles.description: Workspace-relative paths to sibling files the entry depends on (tokens CSS, JSX modules, imported assets), relative to the entry file's directory.

sourceSkillId.description: The skillId used to generate this artifact, if any.

designSystemId.description: The designSystemId used to generate this artifact, if any.

collectionId.description: The same collectionId passed to prepare_open_design_brief, if this screen is part of a design collection.

collectionName.description: The same collectionName passed to prepare_open_design_brief, if this screen is part of a design collection.

screenIndex.description: 0-based position of this screen within its collection (0 for the first screen, 1 for the second, ...).

screenRole.description: The same screenRole passed to prepare_open_design_brief, if this screen is part of a design collection.

explorationId.description: The explorationId from prepare_open_design_exploration, if this artifact belongs to a design exploration. Updates its comparison page.

directionId.description: The direction's directionId, for an exploration sketch. Leave it out for a built-out or merged version registered against the exploration.

sources.description: The same source document paths passed to prepare_open_design_brief. Records each source's hash in the manifest and, for HTML, reports numbers on the page that appear in none of the sources so you can check them.

format.description: The canvas format passed to prepare_open_design_brief (or the adaptation's registerArgs), if any. Recorded in the manifest's metadata.format so export, preflight and adaptation use it without repeating it.

resolvedCommentIds.description: Ids of the user's comments (from get_open_design_artifact's openComments) that this edit addressed. They're marked resolved and their pins leave the preview.

answers.description: The same answers passed to prepare_open_design_brief.

assumptions.description: The same assumptions passed to prepare_open_design_brief.

brief.description: What was asked and assumed for this design, stored as the manifest's metadata.brief (the latest replaces the earlier one) so later edits and checks can see it. Leave it out on an edit that changed none of it.

critique.description: The design critic's latest opinion (from the open-design-critique skill), stored as metadata.critique; only the latest is kept and it must be at most 4 KB. checkRunId defaults to the latest saved check run and at to now.

verdict.description: ship (nothing worth a round), polish (one round of the listed fixes) or rework (the direction is wrong).

where.description: Where on the design (section, element, slide, viewport).

findings.description: At most five, ordered by impact.

checkRunId.description: The check run the critic judged.

languageModelTools.name: get_open_design_artifact
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reads back a registered Open Design artifact: its manifest, entry file content, supporting file list, and the user's unaddressed preview comments ('openComments', status open or sent) from the Open Design Artifact Preview editor or the browser preview, with up to 4 comment screenshots attached. Use this to review what was generated, and check 'openComments' before telling the user you're done — address any pending ones, then pass their ids as resolvedCommentIds to register_open_design_artifact. With critique: true it instead returns what the design critic judges (the open-design-critique prompt): the recorded brief, title and skill id, the design system's DESIGN.md, the latest saved check run's findings and screenshot paths, and the last critique, with that run's screenshots attached.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read back an Open Design artifact

entryPath.description: Workspace-relative path to the artifact's entry file.

critique.description: Return the critique input instead of the entry content and comments. Default false.

languageModelTools.name: set_active_design_system
languageModelTools.displayName: Set Active Open Design Design System
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Sets (or clears, if designSystemId is omitted/empty) the active Open Design design system, persisted for this workspace. The active design system is used automatically by prepare_open_design_brief whenever it's called without an explicit designSystemId. Call this when the user says something like 'let's use the Starbucks look from now on' before you've generated anything yet.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Set or clear the active Open Design design system

designSystemId.description: A design system id from list_open_design_design_systems. Omit or pass an empty string to clear the active design system.

languageModelTools.name: remix_open_design_example
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Copies a curated Open Design example artifact (identified by its skillId, which must have remixable: true from list_open_design_skills) into the workspace as a starting point, registers it as an artifact, and returns instructions telling you to MODIFY the copied file rather than regenerate it from scratch. Use this when the user wants to start from or riff on an existing example rather than build something brand new.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Remix a curated Open Design example into the workspace

skillId.description: A skillId from list_open_design_skills with remixable: true.

languageModelTools.name: create_open_design_design_system
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Composes instructions for authoring a brand-new, custom design system as a DESIGN.md file plus a sibling tokens.css following the Open Design token contract (the same file shape and selection mechanism as the ~150 bundled design systems, just workspace-local). Does NOT write any files. If sourceUrl is given, performs a best-effort, no-daemon extraction of candidate colors/fonts/favicon from that page to include as a starting point. After writing the returned instructions' files, call set_active_design_system with the returned id. To write ONLY a tokens.css for an existing custom design system (id starting with user:), pass existingDesignSystemId instead of name/brief.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Create a custom Open Design design system for your own brand

name.description: A short name for the design system, e.g. "Acme Corp". Required unless existingDesignSystemId is given.

brief.description: A description of the brand — colors, tone, industry, anything distinctive — in the user's own words. Required unless existingDesignSystemId is given.

sourceUrl.description: Optional: a website URL to take a rough starting palette and fonts from, by reading its source. For a design system that matches a site, call extract_open_design_design_system first instead: it renders the page and measures it.

existingDesignSystemId.description: Optional: the id of an existing custom design system (user:…). Returns instructions to write only its tokens.css, from its current DESIGN.md; name, brief and sourceUrl are then ignored.

languageModelTools.name: extract_open_design_design_system
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Renders a website in an installed Chrome, Edge or Chromium and measures its design system: colour roles from the elements that carry them (page background, cards, text, borders, the primary button and its forced :hover/:active states), declared CSS custom properties, the fonts it loaded, text sizes, radii, spacing, container width and motion. Writes an evidence bundle (evidence.json, screenshots, one crop per role, the logo) under <output folder>/.extract/<site>/ and returns a draft token set on the Open Design token contract, with where each value came from and which tokens nothing measured. Does NOT write DESIGN.md or tokens.css: write both from the draft, keeping measured values as measured (the open-design-design-system-from-url prompt has the steps), then save it as a custom design system. Only public http(s) pages; at most 4 pages, 20 seconds each; no logins, cookies or form submissions. A bot check, login wall or empty page comes back as blocked with its screenshot. With no browser installed, falls back to reading the page source and marks the result partial.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Measure a website's colours, fonts and spacing as a starting design system

url.description: The page to measure, e.g. the home page.

extraUrls.description: Optional: up to 3 more pages on the same site (a product or pricing page) to fill in roles the first page lacks.

theme.description: Which theme to measure (default light). dark and both measure a dark theme only if the site has one.

languageModelTools.name: port_open_design_artifact_to_app
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Composes instructions for porting a finished Open Design artifact's design into this workspace's actual, existing application as real, idiomatic production code (not a standalone file). Does NOT write any files. Reads the artifact's current content and, if the app has a recognizable components directory, suggests a target file path. The returned instructions direct the model to find and follow a real existing component in the workspace as its pattern reference (styling approach, conventions, file organization) rather than copying the artifact's HTML/CSS verbatim, and to leave routing/navigation wiring out of scope as a separate step for the user.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Port a finished Open Design artifact into the app's real code

entryPath.description: The workspace-relative path of the artifact to promote (as passed to register_open_design_artifact).

targetComponentPath.description: Optional: where the new component/code file should be written. If omitted, a best-effort suggestion is returned instead.

referenceComponentPath.description: Optional: an existing component file to use as the authoritative pattern for the app's real conventions. If omitted, the model is instructed to find one itself.

languageModelTools.name: prepare_open_design_component_library
languageModelTools.displayName: Build a Component Set from a Design
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Composes staged instructions for turning reviewed Open Design artifacts into a reusable component set on a named React library: Material UI themed to Material 3 ("mui") or shadcn/ui ("shadcn"). Use it when the user asks for components, a component library or a component set from a design; for putting one page into the app, use port_open_design_artifact_to_app instead. Returns a repeated-element inventory to turn into components.md (then stop for the user's approval), a ready theme generated from the design system's tokens, component and gallery rules, and how to record the set. Does NOT write app code. Call it again with record after the set builds: that writes metadata.componentLibrary on the artifacts' manifests so a later run updates the same set.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Turn a reviewed design into a reusable MUI or shadcn component set

entryPaths.description: Workspace-relative entry paths of 1 to 10 registered artifacts the set is built from.

collectionId.description: Instead of entryPaths: every screen of this collection.

library.description: "mui" (Material UI, themed to Material 3), "shadcn" (shadcn/ui), or "auto" (default) to pick from the app's package.json.

outputDir.description: Optional: workspace-relative folder for the components, inside the app. Default: <app>/src/components/<DesignName>, or the folder an earlier record names.

record.description: Stage 5 only: the finished set, written to the artifacts' manifests instead of returning instructions.

languageModelTools.name: share_open_design_artifact_to_community
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Composes instructions for packaging a finished Open Design artifact as a new entry in the community-contributed design catalog (awesome-open-design). Does NOT write any files and does NOT run any commands itself. The returned instructions direct the model to: (1) derive a slug/title/description/example_prompt from the artifact itself rather than asking the user to retype anything, (2) scaffold a local SKILL.md + example.html + open-design.json folder with its own file-editing tools, (3) explicitly check in with the user before publishing anything, since that step is public and hard to reverse, and only then (4) fork/branch/push/open a PR against the community repo using its own terminal tool under the user's own already-authenticated gh/git identity — never inventing a placeholder GitHub owner if gh auth is missing.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Share a finished Open Design artifact to the community design catalog

entryPath.description: The workspace-relative path of the artifact to share (as passed to register_open_design_artifact).

languageModelTools.name: publish_open_design_artifact_to_canva
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Gets a finished Open Design artifact into Canva. Called with entryPath alone, it composes instructions and writes nothing. The instructions have you export the artifact (PDF, or PPTX for a deck), check whether the user's Canva MCP server is connected (via list_open_design_integrations), and then: when Canva is connected, let the user choose between an editable import (the export is hosted briefly on a public link with publish_open_design_artifact, then Canva's import-design-from-url converts it into a design, optionally published as a Brand Template after their yes) and a private upload into their Canva Uploads; when it isn't, offer setup once and otherwise give them Canva's manual Import a file steps. For the private upload, call it again with filePath (the export) and uploadUrl (from Canva's create-upload-url): the server then POSTs the file's bytes to that canva.com URL from the machine the file is on, so no terminal is needed, and returns the fileId. Use when the user wants an artifact in Canva, as a Canva design or a Canva template.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get a finished Open Design artifact into Canva (through the Canva connector when it's connected)

entryPath.description: The workspace-relative path of the artifact to prepare for Canva (as passed to register_open_design_artifact).

filePath.description: The exported file to upload (route B), workspace-relative as export_open_design_artifact returned it; must be in the artifact's exports/ folder. Pass with uploadUrl.

uploadUrl.description: The single-use upload URL from Canva's create-upload-url (https, canva.com). With filePath, the server uploads the file there instead of returning instructions.

languageModelTools.name: publish_open_design_artifact_to_shop
languageModelTools.displayName: Put Open Design Designs in a Shop
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Gets finished shop designs into the user's online shop: the product images (and any other design filled per product) from the product list. For shop "shopify" it composes instructions and writes nothing: check whether Shopify's connector is connected (via list_open_design_integrations and your own tools), and if it is, show the product matches first, make the first three updates one at a time with the user's go-ahead, create new products only as drafts, leave price, stock and visibility alone unless asked, attach images only if a connector tool can, and report what changed per product. Otherwise, and for bigcartel, etsy and other shops, it exports each design once per product and writes <design folder>/for-<shop>/: images named <product>-1.png, <product>-2.png…, copy.md with each product's title, price and description, and for Shopify a products.csv in Shopify's import format (unpublished, image links empty), plus the shop's own upload steps to pass on. Cost, margin, supplier, stock and note columns are never used. This tool never contacts the shop.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Put product images and copy into Shopify, Big Cartel or Etsy: through Shopify's connector, or as a folder ready to upload

entryPaths.description: Workspace-relative entry files of the registered designs to put in the shop, each with [data-od-field] fields filled per product (e.g. the product image, then a second angle). Their images become <product>-1, <product>-2… in that order.

data.description: Workspace-relative product list (CSV, XLSX or JSON array), one row per product: the same list the designs were exported with. Needed for the folder.

nameField.description: The column holding each product's title. Default: a title, name or product column.

folder.description: Shopify only: write the hand-off folder now instead of the connector instructions (when the connector isn't connected, the user declined it, or it can't attach images). Other shops always get the folder.

languageModelTools.name: pull_open_design_figma_frame
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Composes instructions for translating a Figma frame into a real code artifact with 1:1 visual fidelity. When the user's Figma MCP server is connected (checked via list_open_design_integrations), the instructions use Figma's own get_design_context, get_variable_defs and get_screenshot; no token needed. A Figma personal access token is optional: when one is configured, the frame's structural summary and a rendered image are fetched too and included as ground truth, and it's the fallback when Figma isn't connected. Does NOT write any files — author the entry file yourself with your normal file-editing tools, then call register_open_design_artifact. figmaUrl must be a frame-scoped link (Figma's "Copy link to selection", with node-id), not a bare file link.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Translate a Figma frame into a code artifact

figmaUrl.description: A Figma frame URL, e.g. from "Copy link to selection" — must include a node-id.

designSystemId.description: Optional design system id from list_open_design_design_systems to align the translated code with.

languageModelTools.name: push_open_design_artifact_to_figma
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Pushes a finished Open Design artifact into Figma as editable layers through the user's Figma MCP server. Renders the artifact in a headless browser and captures its layers (or reuses a capture newer than the file), then writes ready-to-run code parts and image files under the artifact's exports/figma/ and returns instructions: check Figma is connected (list_open_design_integrations), ask the user whether to add to an existing Figma file (a link) or create a new one, load Figma's figma-use guidance, run each part with Figma's use_figma exactly as written, upload the images with upload_assets, then verify with get_screenshot and share the link. Never contacts Figma itself. When Figma isn't connected, the instructions offer setup and otherwise give the OD Figma Import plugin steps. Use when the user wants a design in Figma ("push this to Figma", "get this into Figma", "hand this off to design").
languageModelTools.userDescription: Push a finished Open Design artifact into Figma as editable layers (through the Figma connection)

entryPath.description: The workspace-relative path of the artifact's entry file (as passed to register_open_design_artifact).

refresh.description: Re-capture the artifact even when a capture newer than the file exists (for example after changing assets the capture can't see).

languageModelTools.name: export_open_design_artifact
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Renders a registered Open Design artifact in a headless browser (an installed Chrome, Edge, or Chromium) and writes upload-ready file(s) under the artifact's own exports/ folder. Does not modify the artifact's source files. IMAGES (png/jpeg): use after register_open_design_artifact whenever the user wants an image to post (X, Instagram, Xiaohongshu, a YouTube thumbnail, a poster). Size comes from explicit width/height, else the source skill's aspect hint, else each selected element's box, else 1080×1080. For multi-card designs mark each card with data-od-card and pass selector "[data-od-card]" for one numbered image per card. Pass maxBytes with the platform's upload limit (X 5000000, YouTube thumbnail 2000000, Instagram 8000000) and images are re-encoded as JPEG until they fit. DECKS: format "pptx" gives a PowerPoint file with one full-bleed slide image per slide (pixel-perfect, not editable text); format "pdf" gives one page per slide. Slides are captured at the deck's own measured slide size, at scale 2 by default. Artifacts registered with kind "deck" (or made from an od:deck:* skill) are detected automatically; pass deck: true if a deck was registered as "html". Pass slides (1-based numbers) with format png/jpeg to export just those slides as images. PAGES: format "pdf" on an ordinary page prints it with the browser's print engine (vector, selectable text, A4 unless the page's CSS sets a size). PACKAGING (no browser needed): format "standalone" writes one self-contained .html with the page's local CSS, scripts, images and fonts inlined, to attach or send; format "site" writes a deploy-ready folder (exports/site/) — to put a design online, prefer publish_open_design_artifact, which builds it for you. Not for video — HyperFrames videos are rendered with the HyperFrames CLI per the brief's instructions. POSTERS AND PREFLIGHT: page exports run preflight checks (text overflow, safe area, print bleed size, minimum type size, contrast, emoji, image resolution for print, QR codes that don't decode, broken assets) and list findings, errors first; findings never block the export. Pass checkOnly: true to check without writing files, and fix every error before the real export. Pass preset with a format id ("ig-portrait", "story", "a3"…) rather than width/height/selector/maxBytes. Pass data with a spreadsheet to export one poster, card or certificate per row. FLUID POSTERS (cards with data-od-fluid): preset reflows the design to that shape in the rendered page (the file is unchanged); presets exports several shapes at once; shapeSheet shows them all in one image. EMAIL AND PASTE: format "email" writes an inbox-safe email (and checks for what breaks in Gmail and Outlook: flex/grid layout, SVG, transforms, local images, missing alt, width over 640px, size over 102 KB); format "paste" with target wechat|notion|newsletter|generic writes an inlined fragment. Both compute styles in the browser, so Tailwind or any runtime CSS is inlined. To use the result, the user opens the file in a browser, selects all, copies and pastes. VIDEO AND GIF: format "mp4", "webm" or "gif" renders animated HTML (CSS animations, requestAnimationFrame, timers, data-duration storyboards, WebGL) frame by frame and encodes it with an installed ffmpeg (never downloaded; a 'no-ffmpeg' or 'ffmpeg-missing-encoder' error says what to install). Up to 60 seconds. Use maxBytes for platform limits (re-encodes smaller). HyperFrames compositions still render with the HyperFrames CLI.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Export an Open Design artifact to PNG/JPEG, PDF, PPTX, standalone HTML, an HTML email or paste-ready HTML

entryPath.description: Workspace-relative path to the registered artifact's entry file.

format.description: Output format. png/jpeg: images; pdf: deck slides or a printed page; pptx: decks only; standalone: one self-contained .html (to attach or send); site: a deploy-ready folder. Default png. email: an inbox-ready HTML email (exports/<name>.email.html, styles inlined, 600px column, preheader, dark-mode meta) plus a plain-text exports/<name>.email.txt, with email preflight; pass baseUrl once the artifact's assets are hosted so image URLs become absolute. paste: an inlined HTML fragment to paste into another editor (exports/<name>.<target>.html); needs target. mp4, webm, gif: animate the page on a virtual clock (frame-exact, the same on every run) and encode it with an installed ffmpeg; size from width/height, preset or the skill, duration from the page unless you pass duration.

width.description: Width in CSS pixels, given with height. Overrides the skill's size for images, the measured slide size for decks, or the print page size for page PDFs.

height.description: Viewport height in CSS pixels. Give together with width.

scale.description: Device scale factor (1–3). Default 2 for deck pptx/pdf (crisp when projected), 1 otherwise.

selector.description: CSS selector; each matching element is exported as its own numbered image (e.g. "[data-od-card]").

maxBytes.description: Per-file byte budget; over-budget images are re-encoded as progressively lower-quality JPEG until they fit.

deck.description: Force deck handling (true) or page handling (false). Omit to detect it from the artifact's kind and source skill.

slides.description: Decks only: 1-based slide numbers to export, e.g. [1, 3]. With png/jpeg, one image per slide; with pdf/pptx, only these slides in this order.

badge.description: standalone/site only: add a small, closeable "Made with Open Design" footer badge. Default: on for site, off for standalone; the openDesign.share.badge setting turns it off.

baseUrl.description: site only: the https address the bundle will be served from, so the link-preview image (og:image) can be an absolute URL. For email and paste: relative image and link URLs are rewritten against it.

embedAssets.description: standalone only: download the remote assets the page declares (a 3d-scene spec's assets, or an application/od-assets+json block: HDRIs, textures, glTF models with their files) and embed them in the page, so it works where other sites are blocked (a Claude artifact) or offline. The result lists each embedded asset and the page size; above 16 MB the export fails, naming the largest. An asset that can't be downloaded is reported and left as its URL.

maxResolution.description: With embedAssets: the highest Poly Haven resolution to fetch for textures and HDRIs (1k, 2k or 4k; default 1k). Models keep the resolution the page uses.

preset.description: A canvas format id instead of hand-copied sizes. Screen formats (x-image (1600×900), ig-square (1080×1080 per card), ig-portrait (1080×1350), story (1080×1920), xhs-card (1080×1440 per card), yt-thumbnail (1280×720), linkedin-image (1200×627), og-image (1200×630), x-header (1500×500), linkedin-banner (1584×396), email-header (600×200, captured at 2×), and display ads banner-mrec (300×250), banner-leaderboard (728×90), banner-skyscraper (160×600), banner-mobile (320×50), and shop images shop-product (2048×2048), shop-banner (1920×800), shop-collection (1920×600)) fill in width/height, selector "[data-od-card]" and the platform's byte budget. Print formats (a4, a3, a2, a1, a0, a5, a6, a7, letter, tabloid, poster-18x24, poster-24x36, postcard-4x6, business-card, business-card-us, and cards with rounded corners trading-card, tarot-card, mini-card) produce a print-ready PDF the size of the bleed box, with TrimBox and BleedBox set. Explicit arguments still win. Without preset, the format the artifact was registered with is used.

bleed.description: Print PDFs only: bleed in mm on every side. Default: the format's (3 mm for ISO sizes, 3.175 mm for US sizes). The card must be authored at trim size plus this bleed.

cropMarks.description: Print PDFs only: add crop marks at the trim corners in a 10 mm slug around the page.

dpi.description: Print images only (PNG or JPEG of a print format): the resolution, 150–600 (default 300). The image is the bleed box at this dpi, and the dpi is written into the file. Can't be combined with scale; over 8192 px a side is refused, naming the largest dpi that fits.

printHouse.description: A print-house profile id from list_open_design_print_houses, e.g. "boardgamesmaker". Writes each card face at that printer's exact upload size and file type (bleed included, only bleed removed), with -front/-back names and one back per card when the printer asks for it. The design's format must be one the printer takes. Can't be combined with dpi, scale, width/height, presets or selector.

checkOnly.description: Run the page load and preflight checks only, writing no files and leaving the manifest alone. Use it to check and fix a design before exporting.

data.description: Workspace-relative CSV, XLSX or JSON-array file. For each row, [data-od-field="<column>"] elements are filled (text, or src on img, href on a) and [data-od-qr-field="<column>"] gets a QR code, in the rendered page only (the file isn't changed). Images: one file per row; PDFs: one multi-page file (or split). At most 200 rows; every field must have a column.

sheet.description: XLSX data only: the sheet to read (default: the first).

nameField.description: With data: the column whose value names each row's file (slugified, made unique), e.g. "name" gives poster-ada-lovelace.png. Default: row numbers.

split.description: With data and a PDF format: one PDF per row instead of one multi-page PDF.

presets.description: Fluid designs only: export several canvas shapes in one call, each reflowed and preflighted at its own shape and written as <name>-<format>.<ext> (PDF for print shapes, PNG for screen shapes unless format is given). Can't be combined with preset, width or height. With data: one file per row per shape.

shapeSheet.description: Fluid designs only: also write exports/<name>-shapes.png, one image showing the design at every shape in presets (default: all catalog formats), each labelled and marked when preflight found errors there. With checkOnly: true it is the only file written. Use it to show the user how a poster looks in every size.

campaignSheet.description: Fluid designs: also write exports/campaign-sheet.png — the master at every shape in presets (default: the usual poster and social shapes), plus the first screen of every other piece registered in the master's collection (landing page, email…), each labelled and marked when it has preflight errors. Use it to show the user a whole campaign at a glance. With checkOnly: true it is the only file written.

target.description: format "paste" only: where it will be pasted. wechat: top-level blocks become <section>s for the WeChat Official Account editor. notion: layout wrappers flattened and code-block languages kept, as Notion turns pasted HTML into blocks. newsletter: email rules and checks applied to the fragment. generic: any rich-text editor.

fps.description: mp4/webm/gif only: frames per second. Default 30 (15 for GIF).

duration.description: mp4/webm/gif only: length in seconds. Default: the sum of the frames' data-duration, else the longest CSS/Web animation, else 6.

loop.description: gif only: loop forever. Default true.

transparent.description: png only: capture without the page background, so everything the design doesn't paint is transparent — for cut-outs such as a 3D product shot to place on slides or pages. The page (and a 3D scene's renderer) must have a transparent background; a warning says so when every pixel came out opaque. PNGs aren't re-encoded to fit maxBytes when transparent.

languageModelTools.name: check_open_design_artifact
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Renders a registered Open Design artifact in a headless browser (an installed Chrome, Edge, or Chromium) and returns what it looks like: screenshots attached as images, plus preflight findings (overflow and clipped text, contrast, text overlap, safe area, broken images/fonts, emoji, QR codes, and horizontal-scroll for pages that scroll sideways), taste warnings (slop-glow, card-row, uniform-surface, type-scale, intent: fix them unless the brief or design system asks for that look) and, for pages, accessibility in hover and focus states, tap targets, reflow at 320 px and reduced motion. Writes no files and leaves the manifest alone. Call it after creating or substantially editing an artifact and registering it, before telling the user it's done: fix every ERROR, look at the screenshots for what the checks can't measure (balance, hierarchy, crowded or empty areas, text over busy imagery), then re-check — at most two fix rounds; tell the user about anything left. For a 3D design with a review sheet, a clean check isn't the end: get the critique the result asks for, for up to three critique rounds. What it renders: a page without a [data-od-card] at each viewport (default desktop 1440×900 and mobile 390×844, findings tagged by viewport); a card design (poster, social post) at its registered format size; a deck slide by slide (findings tagged by slide, one contact sheet of up to 12 slides — pass slides to see others). Screenshots are JPEG with a long edge of at most 1568 px; maxImages (default 3, max 6) bounds how many are attached, and 0 returns findings only. Returns a 'no-browser' error when no browser is installed: then skip the check and tell the user once that visual checking needs Chrome, Edge or Chromium. For bulk data rows or shape sheets, use export_open_design_artifact with checkOnly instead. A 3D scene that exposes window.odScene.scene, camera and renderer (the 3d-object ready contract) also gets a review sheet, one image showing the overview, close-up, low-angle and wireframe views (placed second), plus 3D evidence (pixel metrics, renderer statistics) and a webgl-budget warning for scenes too heavy for software rendering; views picks which views go on the sheet, or false for none.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Render an Open Design artifact and check how it looks (screenshots plus preflight findings)

entryPath.description: Workspace-relative path to the registered artifact's entry file.

views.description: 3D scenes exposing window.odScene.scene/camera/renderer: which review views to put on the sheet (default all four: overview, closeup, low, wireframe), or false for no sheet.

states.description: Pages: also force hover and keyboard focus on up to 60 interactive elements (state-contrast, focus-visible), measure tap targets at phone widths (tap-target), render at 320 px wide (reflow) and with reduced motion (reduced-motion). Default true; false for a faster check.

viewports.description: Pages without a card only: 1–4 viewports to check instead of the default desktop 1440×900 and mobile 390×844.

name.description: Label used in findings and screenshots, e.g. "tablet".

slides.description: Decks only: 1-based slide numbers to check (default every slide; the contact sheet shows the first 12 of them).

maxImages.description: How many screenshots to attach (default 3). 0 returns findings only.

at.description: Animations: up to 6 times in seconds. Also captures the artifact at those moments on a virtual clock (labelled t=<seconds>s), so you can see the start, middle and end of an animation. They share maxImages with the regular screenshots.

languageModelTools.name: find_open_design_3d_assets
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches Poly Haven (polyhaven.com) for free CC0 3D assets and returns the direct CDN file URLs a three.js page needs: an HDRI (.hdr, for real environment light and reflections), a PBR texture set (diffuse, normal, roughness, AO/roughness/metal JPGs) or a model (.gltf plus its included files). Use it in 3D designs when procedural shapes and RoomEnvironment aren't enough: a stone floor, a wood table, a sky, a lantern, a chair. Each result has its id, name, categories, size in meters for models, a thumbnail, the file URLs at 1k (default) or 2k, the license (CC0: no attribution needed) and a 'Powered by Poly Haven' credit. Load the files straight from their URLs (the CDN allows it) or download them into the design's assets/ for offline use; for a model, map its includes with a LoadingManager URL modifier. Writes nothing. If Poly Haven can't be reached, it says so: fall back to procedural materials.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Find free CC0 HDRIs, textures and models on Poly Haven for a 3D design

query.description: What to find, in a few words: a material ("cobblestone", "oak floor"), an object ("lantern", "armchair") or a sky ("sunset field", "overcast").

type.description: hdri for environment light and sky, texture for a PBR surface, model for an object.

resolution.description: File resolution (default 1k; 2k only for the hero object).

languageModelTools.name: adapt_open_design_artifact
languageModelTools.displayName: Adapt Open Design Artifact to Other Formats
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Re-composes a finished, registered design for other canvas formats: the same message, copy hierarchy and design system, laid out again for each new size rather than scaled. Use when the user wants a poster or post "in other sizes", "for Instagram and Stories too", "as an A3 print as well", and so on. Returns, per format, instructions (with the master's HTML, that format's canvas rules and re-composition rules), a suggested entry path and the exact arguments to register it with. Writes no design file: write each adaptation yourself, register it with its registerArgs, then preflight and export it with its preset. The master and its adaptations are grouped as one collection (the master is added to a new one if it isn't in one). FLUID designs (data-od-fluid) already reflow to every shape, so for them it returns mode "tune" instead: per shape, instructions to check the master at that shape and fix it in place with @container rules; no new files and no collection.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Re-compose a design for other sizes (social formats, print)

entryPath.description: Workspace-relative path to the registered master design's entry file.

formats.description: 1–6 target canvas formats. Screen: x-image (1600×900), ig-square (1080×1080 per card), ig-portrait (1080×1350), story (1080×1920), xhs-card (1080×1440 per card), yt-thumbnail (1280×720), linkedin-image (1200×627), og-image (1200×630), x-header (1500×500), linkedin-banner (1584×396), email-header (600×200, captured at 2×), and display ads banner-mrec (300×250), banner-leaderboard (728×90), banner-skyscraper (160×600), banner-mobile (320×50), and shop images shop-product (2048×2048), shop-banner (1920×800), shop-collection (1920×600). Print: a4, a3, a2, a1, a0, a5, a6, a7, letter, tabloid, poster-18x24, poster-24x36, postcard-4x6, business-card, business-card-us, and cards with rounded corners trading-card, tarot-card, mini-card.

notes.description: Optional: what the user said about the adaptations (e.g. "keep the photo on the story").

languageModelTools.name: create_open_design_qr_code
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Generates a real, scannable QR code offline as SVG and saves it in a registered artifact's assets/ folder (listed in its manifest's supportingFiles), returning inline SVG markup to paste into the design. Use whenever a design needs a QR code (event sign-up, menu, ticket, download link); never draw a fake or placeholder one. The markup carries data-od-qr, so export preflight decodes the rendered code and checks it. For one code per row of a spreadsheet, mark the slot with data-od-qr-field="<column>" and export with data instead.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Create a real, scannable QR code for a design

entryPath.description: Workspace-relative path to the registered artifact the code belongs to.

text.description: What the code encodes, usually a full https URL.

name.description: File name for the SVG under assets/ (default "qr"), e.g. "signup-qr".

errorCorrection.description: Error correction level. Default M; use H when a logo will be placed over the code.

margin.description: Quiet zone in modules (default 4, the standard; don't go below 2).

languageModelTools.name: add_open_design_diagram_runtime
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Adds the diagram runtime to a diagram's HTML entry file, or updates it in place: one inline <script data-od-runtime="diagram"> block, placed before </body>, that lays the diagram out in the browser. It places nodes on a grid by rank and lane, draws right-angle connectors through the gaps between them with arrowheads and labels, boxes groups, and lays out sequence diagrams. The same file then renders identically in the preview, in export, in check_open_design_artifact and in any browser. Call it after writing the diagram markup (the diagram skill's workflow says when); it works before or after register_open_design_artifact and changes nothing else in the file. Never write, copy or edit the runtime yourself. The result restates the markup contract: a container with data-od-diagram (data-direction right|down, or ="sequence"); nodes with data-od-node, data-rank, data-lane, optional data-group and data-od-source; hidden <i data-od-link data-from data-to data-label> links; hidden <i data-od-group data-label> groups; for sequences, data-od-participant elements and hidden <i data-od-message data-from data-to data-label data-kind="return"> messages.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add or update the layout runtime in a diagram

entryPath.description: Workspace-relative path to the diagram's HTML entry file.

languageModelTools.name: publish_open_design_artifact
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Publishes a registered Open Design artifact as a live web page, so the user can share a link with teammates or stakeholders. Use when the user asks to share, publish, deploy, host or "get a link" for a design. (For a single file to attach or send, use export_open_design_artifact with format "standalone" instead.) It builds a deploy-ready folder (exports/site/) locally, then returns step-by-step instructions for publishing it with the host's own CLI from your terminal, under the user's own login or a temporary no-account link: netlify-temporary or cloudflare-temporary (no account, about 60 minutes unless claimed), or netlify, vercel, cloudflare-pages or github-pages (the user's own account). It never deploys anything itself and never handles tokens. Without provider, the instructions ask the user to choose. The instructions require the user's explicit yes before anything goes online. With provider claude-artifact (only if you have an Artifact tool: Claude Code or Claude Desktop), it writes the standalone file instead, checks it against the artifact viewer's limits, and returns instructions to publish that file by path with your Artifact tool; the artifact stays private until the user shares it, so there is no confirmation step. After a successful deploy or publish, call this tool again with published: { provider, url, claimUrl?, expiresAt?, siteRef? } to record the link, so the next publish updates the same site or artifact.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Publish an Open Design artifact as a shareable web link

entryPath.description: Workspace-relative path to the registered artifact's entry file.

provider.description: Where to publish. Omit to get the choices to show the user.

badge.description: Add the small, closeable "Made with Open Design" footer badge to the published page. Default true; the openDesign.share.badge setting turns it off.

includeFiles.description: Workspace paths of files in this artifact's own exports/ folder (e.g. an exported PDF) to host alongside the page, at files/<name> in the bundle, publicly downloadable at <site URL>/files/<name>. Used by the Canva flow to give Canva a URL to import. Export the files first.

published.description: Record mode: what the deploy reported. Doesn't rebuild anything.

url.description: The public https link, or the https://claude.ai/... artifact link.

claimUrl.description: Temporary providers: the https link the user claims the site with. It's private to the user.

expiresAt.description: Temporary providers: ISO date-time when the link stops working unless claimed.

siteRef.description: Site id, project name or owner/repo/folder to redeploy to next time.

languageModelTools.name: list_open_design_integrations
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Looks up trusted third-party MCP servers (Canva, Figma, Notion, Google Drive, Slack, posting services such as Buffer and Metricool, X's official server) that a workflow step can use instead of a manual handoff. Call it whenever a step would hand work to another service (import into Canva, read a Figma frame, save to Drive, share in Slack, post to a social network). With no arguments it returns the catalog of capabilities and integrations. With capability, integration and/or platform it returns the providers in priority order (official platform server, then official service, then posting services), the tool-name patterns that show each one is installed, the setup steps for this agent, and the consent rules. Check your own tools (including deferred ones) against those patterns: if one is installed, use it by its server-defined tool name. If none is, offer setup once and only proceed after the user says yes; never install silently, never ask for or write API keys. If the user declines, continue with the workflow's manual path. This tool only returns text: it installs nothing and contacts no service.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Find the trusted integrations (Canva, Figma, Notion, Drive, Slack, social posting) a design workflow can use, with setup steps

capability.description: What the step needs, e.g. "design.import", "design.read", "storage.upload", "team.share", "social.post". Call with no arguments to see every capability.

platform.description: Social network, for social.* capabilities: x, linkedin, instagram, facebook, threads, tiktok, youtube, pinterest, bluesky, mastodon.

agent.description: Which agent the setup steps are for. Defaults to vscode here.

languageModelTools.name: list_open_design_print_houses
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the card and sticker printers whose upload sizes the kit knows: each one's id, the formats it takes with the exact pixel size, file type and dpi, how it wants card backs, and the page those sizes came from with the date they were checked. Call it when the user names a printer or says the cards are going to a print house; pass the id as printHouse to export_open_design_artifact. When their printer isn't listed, export print images at 300 dpi and tell them to check the size against the printer's upload page. Read-only.
languageModelTools.userDescription: See which card and sticker printers' upload sizes the kit knows, to export cards ready to upload

openDesign.outputDirectory.markdownDescription: Workspace-relative directory new Open Design artifacts are suggested under, e.g. `.open-design/<slug>/index.html`.

openDesign.activeDesignSystemId.markdownDescription: The currently active Open Design design system id. Used as the default for `prepare_open_design_brief` when no `designSystemId` is given. Set via the "Open Design: Browse Design Systems" command, the `set_active_design_system` tool, or by generating with an explicit design system — leave empty for none.

openDesign.communityContentEnabled.markdownDescription: Whether to fetch and show community-contributed remixable designs from [awesome-open-design](https://github.com/feimacode/awesome-open-design) alongside the built-in gallery. This content is not reviewed by the extension author. Fetched automatically once on first activation, and re-synced any time via the "Open Design: Sync Community Designs" command.

openDesign.communityContentRef.markdownDescription: The tag of [awesome-open-design](https://github.com/feimacode/awesome-open-design) to fetch community designs from. Change this, then run "Open Design: Sync Community Designs", to track a different release.

openDesign.export.browserPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to a Chrome, Edge, or Chromium executable used to export artifacts to PNG/JPEG. Leave empty to auto-detect an installed browser (or set the `OPEN_DESIGN_BROWSER_PATH` environment variable).

openDesign.export.ffmpegPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to an `ffmpeg` executable used to export animations as MP4, WebM or GIF. Leave empty to auto-detect an installed one (or set the `OPEN_DESIGN_FFMPEG_PATH` environment variable). ffmpeg is never downloaded.

openDesign.experimental.servedPreview.markdownDescription: Experimental. Show designs in the preview's View mode from a local server (bound to `127.0.0.1`, behind a random path) instead of as embedded text, so they behave exactly as in a browser: tab switches, relative files and scripts all work. Comment, Edit and Tweaks still use the embedded copy. In a remote window the port is forwarded through VS Code.

openDesign.share.badge.markdownDescription: Add a small, closeable "Made with Open Design · Remix this" footer badge to pages you publish (`publish_open_design_artifact`, export format `site`). It loads nothing from the internet and doesn't track viewers. Turn this off to never add it; a single publish can still leave it out with `badge: false`. Standalone HTML downloads never get it unless asked.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Open Design
walkthroughs.description: Design decks, pages, dashboards and social posts in Copilot Chat, using Open Design's skills and brand design systems.

steps.title: Generate your first design
steps.description:
Describe what you want in Copilot Chat (agent mode). Copilot picks a recipe, writes the files and opens a live preview.
[Try a sample request](command:workbench.action.chat.open?%7B%22query%22%3A%20%22Make%20me%20a%20pitch%20deck%20for%20a%20Series%20A%20fintech%20startup%2C%20editorial%20style.%22%2C%20%22isPartialQuery%22%3A%20true%7D)

steps.title: Start from a real example
steps.description:
Browse 193 rendered examples and remix one instead of starting blank.
[Open the gallery](command:openDesign.openGalleryGrid)

steps.title: Pick a design system
steps.description:
Choose a brand look once; every design after that follows it.
[Browse design systems](command:openDesign.browseDesignSystems)

steps.title: Make a social media post
steps.description:
Design a post at the right size for X, Instagram, LinkedIn, Xiaohongshu, Stories or YouTube, and export it ready to upload.
[Start a social post](command:workbench.action.chat.open?%7B%22query%22%3A%20%22/open-design-social-post%20%22%2C%20%22isPartialQuery%22%3A%20true%7D)

steps.title: Export images, PDF or PowerPoint
steps.description:
Turn any design into PNG or JPEG, a deck into PowerPoint or PDF, or a page into a PDF.
[Open the docs](command:openDesign.openDocs)

scripts.lint: eslint src --ext ts && npm run check-sync --workspace=@feimacode/open-design-agent-kit-content && node scripts/check-content-mirror.mjs
scripts.test:unit: npm run compile && node --import tsx --test src/test/*.test.ts
